summary: Lists requirements for a new IETF tool that Area Directors would use to create, re-charter, and close working groups, and that the wider community could use to see how chartering is going. It is input for later design work, not a protocol, and is informational only.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 6292 lists requirements for a tool to manage IETF working-group charters. It covers the review process, record keeping, decisions, and public access to charter information.

questions: ietf working group charter tool requirements

subtitle: Requirements for a tool to manage IETF working-group chartering, rechartering, and closure.

tldr.problem: Creating, changing, and closing IETF working groups relied heavily on manual requests and updates by Area Directors and Secretariat staff.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists requirements for working-group records, review states, charter ballots, closure requests, public search, comparisons, and an Atom feed.
tldr.outcome: This is a requirements document intended as input to tool design and development, not a protocol. It has been updated by RFC 6433.

today: RFC 6292 is an Informational requirements document and has been updated by RFC 6433. It does not define a protocol.

sections.title: The Chartering Process
sections.content:
RFC 2418 describes how IETF working groups are formed and operated. At the time RFC 6292 was written, creating, rechartering, and closing groups involved manual requests and updates to the Secretariat database and Datatracker.

This document lists requirements for a proposed tool. Creating and rechartering groups involve internal and external review and likely IESG approval. Closing a group does not require IESG review or approval. Milestone changes are outside the charter process described here.
sections.plainLanguage: The document describes a tool to reduce manual work when IETF groups start, change their charters, or close. It treats closure differently because that action does not require IESG review.

sections.title: Working-Group Records and Comments
sections.content:
The tool keeps a record for each proposed group and for each existing group whose charter is under review. A record includes the group name and acronym, chairs, secretary, technical advisors, responsible Area Director, area, charter text, mailing list, related sites, prior acronyms, and the reason for the charter.

Area Directors can edit record fields and set the review state. Comments can be marked as blocking or non-blocking. Charter text proposals are stored with names that preserve their order and history.
sections.plainLanguage: Each group under consideration has a record with its leaders, area, charter, and review status. The record also keeps comments and earlier charter drafts.

sections.title: Review States for a New Group
sections.content:
A new group record begins in Informal IESG review. The usual path continues through Internal review, External review, IESG review, and WG exists. A proposal may instead return for more work or move to Not currently under review.

Changing state can notify the Secretariat to schedule an IESG telechat or send a review announcement. The proposed tool should prompt an Area Director who tries to move forward before the review time has elapsed, while allowing the change after the prompt.
sections.plainLanguage: A new group moves through internal review, community review, and IESG review before approval. The tool tracks the current step and notifies the Secretariat when action is needed.

sections.title: Rechartering, Ballots, and Closure
sections.content:
Rechartering starts from the existing record and allows its fields to be edited. The review states resemble those for a new group, with an indication that the group already exists. The IESG decides whether external review is needed.

The tool needs a ballot process for charter approval, with yes, no, and abstain positions that Area Directors may change. A closure request must ask what to do with active Internet-Drafts, what to say in the closure announcement, and whether the mailing list should remain open.
sections.plainLanguage: Changing an existing charter follows a review path, but the IESG decides whether to ask for external review. A closure request also records what happens to unfinished drafts and the mailing list.

sections.title: Public Search and Change Tracking
sections.content:
Members of the IETF community can view public charter records and search by group name, acronym, review state, responsible Area Director, area, text, or earlier acronyms. They can view snapshots of earlier charter versions and compare proposed or approved versions.

The tool also needs an Atom feed for charter changes. Each feed entry contains the full group record and indicates what changed since the previous entry. The database should be initialized with current and historical records where they can be loaded mostly automatically.
sections.plainLanguage: Community members can search for a group, review earlier charter versions, and compare changes. An Atom feed reports updates to group records.

sections.title: Access and Security
sections.content:
The RFC continues the existing access model in which Area Directors and the Secretariat can perform actions that other community members cannot. The Secretariat can perform all actions available to an Area Director.

The document says that creating a tool to track group charters does not significantly affect Internet security.
sections.plainLanguage: Area Directors and the Secretariat have permission to change records; other community members can view the public information. The RFC identifies no significant Internet security effect from the tool.
